prof.legionary.desc: Service in the legion: steady pay, campaigns and the risk of never coming home.
prof.rhetor.desc: Speeches in court and in the assembly. The road to fame and influence.
prof.gladiator.desc: Fighting in the arena for show. Fame is possible, a long life is rare.
ev.patron_offer.title: A patron
ev.patron_offer.text: A rich Roman offers to make you his client: greet him every morning and support him at elections. In return, protection and gifts.
ev.patron_offer.note: Patronage ran through Roman society: clients greeted their patron each morning, escorted him and voted for him, and he helped them with money and in court.
ev.insula_fire.title: Fire
ev.insula_fire.text: At night the apartment block you live in caught fire. The flames spread fast through the wooden floors.
ev.insula_fire.note: Fires were common in Rome: insulae were tall and cramped, with wooden floors. Augustus created the vigiles, a night watch and fire brigade.
ev.insula_fire.save_goods.success: You managed to carry out the most valuable things.
ev.insula_fire.save_goods.failure: Smoke and fire. You got out burned and with almost nothing.
ev.tax_collector.title: The tax collector
ev.tax_collector.text: The tax collector demands more than is due, and makes no secret that he'll keep some for himself.
ev.tax_collector.note: Taxes in Egypt were collected in great detail: thousands of surviving papyri are receipts, registers and complaints about collectors' abuses.
ev.tax_collector.bribe.success: A little silver, and the collector found a mistake in his records.
ev.tax_collector.bribe.failure: The collector took offense and charged you double.
ev.tax_collector.petition.success: The complaint was accepted. The collector had to back down.
ev.tax_collector.petition.failure: Nobody read the complaint. You had to pay anyway.
ev.low_flood.title: A low flood
ev.low_flood.text: The Nile flood was weak. The fields won't get enough water, and spring will be hungry.
ev.low_flood.note: Egypt's harvest depended entirely on the Nile flood. Its height was measured with nilometers and used to set taxes.
ev.low_flood.hope.success: It worked out: neighbors shared, and prices fell before the stores ran out.
ev.grain_shortage.title: Not enough bread
ev.grain_shortage.text: The grain ships are late, and the price of bread rises every day.
ev.grain_shortage.note: The great cities of antiquity lived on imported grain. Supply disruptions quickly led to hunger and unrest.
ev.grain_shortage.wait.success: The ships arrived before the food ran out.
ev.assembly.title: The Assembly
ev.assembly.text: The ekklesia gathers on the Pnyx hill to decide whether to go to war. Any citizen may speak.
ev.assembly.note: In democratic Athens the supreme body was the assembly of all adult male citizens. Women, slaves and resident foreigners (metics) took no part.
ev.assembly.speak.success: They listened, they nodded, and then they voted the way you proposed.
ev.assembly.speak.failure: They booed you and wouldn't let you finish.
ev.liturgy.title: A liturgy
ev.liturgy.text: As a wealthy citizen, the city requires you to pay for fitting out a warship.
ev.liturgy.note: Liturgies were mandatory public expenses of rich Athenians: equipping a trireme, staging a chorus. One could challenge a richer man who had avoided the duty to an exchange of property (antidosis).
ev.liturgy.antidosis.success: Your rival chose to pay himself.
ev.liturgy.antidosis.failure: Your rival agreed to the exchange. You lost part of your property and respect.
ev.philosopher.title: A philosopher in the agora
ev.philosopher.text: In the square, a man in a worn cloak asks passers-by awkward questions about justice. Young people gather around him.
ev.museum.title: The Mouseion
ev.museum.text: At the Mouseion of Alexandria, scholars study the stars, plants and the human body. You could become one of their students.
ev.museum.note: The Mouseion and the Library of Alexandria, founded by the Ptolemies, were the greatest center of learning of the age. Euclid, Eratosthenes and the physicians Herophilus and Erasistratus worked there.
ev.games.title: Games in the arena
ev.games.text: A Roman noble is putting on games: gladiator fights and beast hunts. Entry is free.
ev.games.note: The first gladiator fights in Rome took place in 264 BC at a funeral. Later, games became a way for politicians to win popular favor.
ev.recruitment_rome.title: The levy
ev.recruitment_rome.text: The legions are recruiting. Service is long, but the pay is regular and veterans get land.
ev.recruitment_rome.note: After the reforms of the late 2nd century BC the legions became professional: volunteers, including the poor, joined for pay and a plot of land on discharge.
ev.recruitment_greek.title: Recruitment
ev.recruitment_greek.text: The army needs men. You could serve for pay and a share of the loot.
ev.g_marathon.title: Marathon
ev.g_marathon.text: A Persian army landed at Marathon. The Athenian hoplites charged at a run and routed it. The city rejoices.
ev.g_marathon.note: The Battle of Marathon in 490 BC was a victory of the Athenians and Plataeans over the Persian force that landed in Attica.
ev.g_salamis.title: The Persians march on Athens
ev.g_salamis.text: King Xerxes' enormous army is advancing on Athens. Themistocles urges the people to leave the city and trust the fleet.
ev.g_salamis.note: In 480 BC the Athenians evacuated to Salamis and Troezen. The Persians burned the Acropolis, but were soon defeated in the naval battle of Salamis.
ev.g_salamis.evacuate: Leave with your family for Salamis
ev.g_salamis.stay.success: You survived. And at Salamis the fleet crushed the Persians.
ev.g_salamis.stay.failure: The Persians took the Acropolis. You barely escaped, and everything you owned burned.
ev.g_peloponnesian.title: War with Sparta
ev.g_peloponnesian.text: War has broken out with Sparta and its allies. Villagers move inside the Long Walls while the enemy ravages the fields of Attica.
ev.g_peloponnesian.note: The Peloponnesian War (431–404 BC) between Athens and Sparta ended in Athens' defeat.
ev.g_athens_plague.title: Plague in Athens
ev.g_athens_plague.text: A terrible disease broke out in the city, crowded with refugees. Whole families are dying.
ev.g_athens_plague.note: The epidemic of 430–426 BC killed an estimated quarter of Athens' population, Pericles among them. What disease it was is still debated.
ev.g_athens_plague.care.failure: You caught it and hovered between life and death for a long time.
ev.g_sicily.title: Disaster in Sicily
ev.g_sicily.text: News arrived: the great fleet and army sent to Sicily have been destroyed. Nearly every family is grieving.
ev.g_sicily.note: The Sicilian Expedition (415–413 BC) ended with the destruction of the Athenian fleet and army at Syracuse.
ev.g_sulla.title: Sulla takes Athens
ev.g_sulla.text: After a long siege, Sulla's Romans burst into the city. Many were killed and houses were looted.
ev.g_sulla.note: In 86 BC Sulla captured Athens, which had sided with King Mithridates of Pontus.
ev.g_alexander.title: Alexander in Egypt
ev.g_alexander.text: The Persian governor surrendered without a fight. The young Macedonian king Alexander sacrificed to the Egyptian gods, and the priests proclaimed him pharaoh.
ev.g_alexander.note: Alexander the Great took Egypt in 332 BC. After his death the country was ruled by the Ptolemaic dynasty.
ev.g_alexander.welcome: Rejoice at the end of Persian rule
ev.g_alexandria.title: A new city by the sea
ev.g_alexandria.text: Alexandria is being built on the coast. Craftsmen and merchants are invited, with promises of work and profit.
ev.g_alexandria.note: Founded in 331 BC, Alexandria quickly became the Ptolemaic capital and one of the largest cities in the world.
ev.g_roman_egypt.title: Egypt becomes Roman
ev.g_roman_egypt.text: Cleopatra is dead. Octavian has declared Egypt a possession of Rome. The new masters are counting land and taxes.
ev.g_roman_egypt.note: After Antony and Cleopatra's defeat at Actium (31 BC), Egypt became a Roman province in 30 BC and Rome's main granary.
ev.g_hannibal.title: Hannibal in Italy
ev.g_hannibal.text: The Carthaginian general Hannibal has crossed the Alps and is crushing Roman armies. The city is raising new legions.
ev.g_hannibal.note: In the Second Punic War (218–201 BC) Rome suffered defeats at the Trebia, Lake Trasimene and Cannae, but held on and won.
ev.g_hannibal.enlist.success: You survived terrible battles and came back a seasoned soldier.
ev.g_carthage.title: Carthage destroyed
ev.g_carthage.text: News arrived: Carthage has been taken and destroyed. Rome celebrates.
ev.g_carthage.note: In 146 BC, at the end of the Third Punic War, the Romans destroyed Carthage.
ev.g_spartacus.title: Spartacus' revolt
ev.g_spartacus.text: Runaway gladiators led by Spartacus have defeated several Roman armies. Thousands of slaves are joining them. Italy is afraid.
ev.g_spartacus.note: Spartacus' revolt (73–71 BC) was crushed by Crassus.
ev.g_spartacus_slave.title: Spartacus is calling
ev.g_spartacus_slave.text: They say Spartacus' army is very close. The slaves whisper at night: run to him or not?
ev.g_spartacus_slave.note: Spartacus' revolt (73–71 BC) was crushed by Crassus; about six thousand captives were crucified along the Appian Way.
ev.g_spartacus_slave.join.success: In the chaos of the defeat you managed to slip away and start a life as a free person.
ev.g_caesar.title: The Ides of March
ev.g_caesar.text: Caesar has been killed in the Senate by conspirators. The city holds its breath: some weep, others talk of liberty restored.
ev.g_caesar.note: Gaius Julius Caesar was killed on 15 March 44 BC. A new civil war soon followed.
ev.g_great_fire.title: The Great Fire
ev.g_great_fire.text: Rome has been burning for days. Whole districts have turned to ash.
ev.g_great_fire.note: The fire of AD 64, under Nero, destroyed a large part of Rome.
ev.g_antonine_plague.title: The Great Plague
ev.g_antonine_plague.text: A disease with rash and fever has come from the East. It spreads from city to city, sparing no one.
ev.g_antonine_plague.note: The Antonine Plague (from AD 165) was an epidemic, possibly smallpox, brought back by troops from the East. It killed millions across the empire.
ev.g_antonine_plague.care.failure: You caught it and hovered between life and death for a long time.
prof.centurion.desc: You command a hundred legionaries. Pay is many times higher, and so is responsibility.
